translations.text: Jerome, the holy priest, wrote a letter about the death of the blessed Mary, the mother of God, to a certain holy virgin named Eustochium, and to her mother Paula, who was a consecrated widow.
For these two women the same Jerome wrote many commentaries, because they were people of holy life and very diligent in the study of books.
This Jerome was a holy priest, fully trained in the Hebrew language, in Greek, and in Latin; and he translated our Bible from the Hebrew books into the Latin language.
He is the foremost interpreter among the Hebrews, the Greeks and the Latins.
He translated seventy-two books of the old law and the new into Latin as a single Bible, besides many other commentaries that he studied deeply and with diligent understanding.
Then at last he composed this letter to the holy widow Paula, to God's virgin Eustochium, her daughter, and to the whole company of virgins who lived with them under a religious rule, saying this:
"Truly, you urge me to tell you how the blessed Mary was taken up on this present day to the heavenly dwelling,
so that your company of virgins may have this gift in the Latin language: how this great feast day should be spent with heavenly praise throughout the course of every year,
and celebrated with spiritual joy, lest the false account that heretics have spread far and wide should come into your hands, and you then accept the made-up lie as a true story."
Truly, from the beginning of the holy gospel you have learned how the archangel Gabriel announced to the blessed virgin Mary the birth of the heavenly Prince,
and they clearly knew the Saviour's miracles, and the service of the blessed mother of God, and the deeds of her life from the four books of the Gospel.
John the Evangelist wrote about Christ's passion that he himself and Mary stood with sorrowful hearts beside the holy cross to which the Saviour was fastened.
Then he said to his own mother, "Woman, behold, here is your son." Then he said to John, "Look now, here stands your mother."
From that day on, John the Evangelist took care of the holy Mary and obeyed her with careful service, as if she were his own mother.
In his mercy, the Lord entrusted the blessed virgin who bore him to the chaste man John, who always remained in chaste virginity;
and for that reason he was especially dear to the Lord, so much so that the Lord was willing to entrust to him that precious treasure, the queen of the whole world;
so that her most pure virginity would be joined to the chaste man in fitting companionship and a pleasant shared life.
In both of them there was the one virtue of unbroken virginity, but in Mary there was another thing as well: in her is fruitful virginity, as in no one else.
In no other person is there virginity if there is fruitfulness, nor fruitfulness if there is intact virginity.
Therefore both Mary's virginity and her fruitfulness are now made holy through the divine birth; and she surpasses all others in virginity and in fruitfulness.
Yet although she was entrusted specially to John's care, after Christ's ascension she lived in common with the company of the apostles,
going in and out among them, and they all served her with great reverence and love, and she told them plainly about everything concerning Christ's incarnation;
because she had learned all of it with certainty from the beginning through the Holy Spirit, and had seen it with her own eyes;
although the apostles understood all things through the same Spirit, and were taught in all truth.
The archangel Gabriel kept her undefiled, and she remained in the care of John and of all the apostles, in that heavenly school,
meditating on God's law, until on this day God took her to the heavenly throne and raised her above the hosts of angels.
No clearer information about her end is read in any book, except that on this day she departed gloriously from the body.
Her tomb can be seen plainly by everyone who looks on it, to this present day, in the middle of the valley of Jehoshaphat.
The valley lies between Mount Zion and the Mount of Olives, and the tomb is shown open and empty, and above it, in her honour, a great church has been raised with wonderful stonework.
No mortal knows how, or at what hour, her holy body was taken from there, or where it was raised to, or whether she rose from death;
yet some teachers have said that her Son, who mightily rose from death on the third day, also raised his mother's body from death and placed it with immortal glory in the kingdom of heaven.
In the same way, very many teachers have written in their books about the people brought back to life who rose from death with Christ, that they were raised up for ever.
Indeed, they declare that the people who were raised would not have been true witnesses of Christ's resurrection unless they had been raised for ever.

We do not deny the eternal resurrection of the blessed Mary. Yet out of caution, keeping to the faith, it is better for us to suppose it than to rashly assert something unknown; in that way we are without any danger.
We read in many places in books that angels very often came at the death of good people and led their souls to heaven with spiritual hymns of praise.
And, what is still clearer, people heard at the death the singing of men and the singing of women, with great light and a sweet fragrance:
in which it is known that the holy men who have come to God's kingdom through good merits receive the souls of other people at their departure and lead them with great joy to rest.

Now if the Saviour often showed such honour at the departure of his saints, and ordered their spirits to be brought to him with heavenly songs of praise, how much more do you think he would want to send the heavenly host today to meet his own mother,
that with immense light and indescribable hymns of praise they led her to the throne of glory that had been prepared for her from the beginning of the world.
There is no doubt that all the glorious host of heaven then wished to rejoice at her coming with indescribable bliss.

Truly, we also believe that the Lord himself came to meet her, and joyfully, with gladness, set her on his throne with him. Indeed, he wished to fulfil in his own person what he commanded in his law, saying thus,
"Honour your father and your mother." He is his own witness that he honoured his Father, just as he said to the Jews,
"I honour my Father, and you dishonour me." In his humanity he honoured his mother when, as the holy gospel says, he was subject to her in his youth.
It is much more to be believed that he honoured his mother with indescribable honour in his kingdom, since in his human nature he was willing to obey her in this life.
This feast day surpasses the mass-days of all other saints beyond comparison, just as much as this holy virgin, God's mother, is beyond comparison with all other virgins.
This feast day comes once a year for us, but for the dwellers in heaven it is unending. The Holy Spirit marvelled at the ascension of this heavenly queen in songs of praise, asking:
"Who is this who ascends here like the rising dawn, as fair as the moon, as chosen as the sun, and as terrible as an army in battle array?"
The Holy Spirit marvelled because he caused all the dwellers in heaven to marvel at this virgin's ascension.
Mary is fairer than the moon, because she shines without any waning of her brightness.
She is chosen like the sun, with the radiance of high virtues, because the Lord, who is the sun of righteousness, chose her to be his mother.
Her journey is compared to an army in battle array, because she was surrounded by holy powers and by hosts of angels.
Concerning this heavenly queen it is said further, through the same Spirit of God; he said,

"I saw the beautiful one, like a dove, rising up over the streams of the rivers, and an indescribable fragrance rose from her garments; and, as in springtime, blossoms of roses and lilies surrounded her."
The blossoms of the roses signify martyrdom by their redness, and the lilies by their whiteness signify the shining purity of intact virginity.
All the chosen ones who went to God through martyrdom or through chastity accompanied the blessed queen, because she herself is both martyr and virgin.
She is as beautiful as a dove, because she loved the innocence that the Holy Spirit signified when he was seen in the likeness of a dove above Christ at his baptism.
Other martyrs suffered martyrdom in their bodies for faith in Christ, but the blessed Mary was not martyred in the body. Instead her soul was greatly tormented with much suffering,
when she stood sorrowful before Christ's cross and saw her dear child fastened to the hard wood with iron nails.
Now she is greater than a martyr, because she suffered in her soul the martyrdom that other martyrs suffered in their bodies.
She loved Christ above all other people, and so her grief for him was also greater than that of other people. She made his death her own death, because his suffering pierced her soul like a sword.
She lacks no holy virtue, no beauty, and no brightness;
And therefore she was surrounded with roses and lilies, so that her virtues were supported by virtues, and her beauty was increased by the beauty of chastity.
God's chosen ones shine in heavenly glory, each according to his merits;
Now it is to be believed that the blessed queen surpasses the others in glory and brightness by as much as her honours are beyond comparison with those of the other saints.
Before his ascension the Lord said that in his Father's house there are many dwellings. Truly we believe that today he has given the most delightful dwelling to his beloved mother.

The glory of God's chosen is measured by their merits, yet there is no complaint or envy in any of them. They all live in true love and high peace, and each rejoices in another's honours as in his own.
I ask you to rejoice in this feast, for today that glorious maiden ascended to the heavens, so that, raised up with Christ beyond all telling, she may reign forever.
The heavenly queen was rescued today from this wicked world. Again I say, rejoice, because she came free from care to the heavenly dwelling.
Let all the world rejoice, because today salvation has been increased for us all through her merits.
Through our ancient mother Eve the gate of the kingdom of heaven was locked against us, and through Mary it has been opened to us again, since she herself gloriously entered it today.
God commanded us through his prophet that we should praise and glorify him in his saints, in whom he is wonderful.
It is much more fitting that on this great feast of his blessed mother we should honour him with hymns and worthy praises, for without doubt all her honour is the praise of God.
Let us therefore now honour this great feast with all the devotion of our minds, for the way to our salvation lies in the praises of our Lord.
Let those who live in virginity rejoice, for they have earned the right to be what they praise. Let them take care to be such that they can praise her worthily.

Let those who live in chaste widowhood praise and honour her, for it is clear that they cannot be chaste except through the grace of Christ, which was present in its fullness in Mary, whom they praise.
Let those who live in marriage also praise and honour her, for from her mercy and grace flow to everyone, so that they may praise her.

If anyone is sinful, let him confess, and by no means praise, although praise is not beautiful in the sinner's mouth; yet let him not cease from that praise, because forgiveness is promised to him by it.
This epistle would take us a great deal of explaining, and it would be very deep for you to hear.
We do not have time now to say more about it, but we will tell some other encouraging story about the great mother of God, for your improvement.
Truly Mary is the greatest comfort and help of Christian people. This has very often been shown, as we read in books.
A certain man was deceived by sorcery, so that he renounced Christ, wrote a pledge in his own hand to the accursed devil, and bound himself to him as his vassal.
His name was Theophilus. Then afterwards he thought better of it, and turned over the torment of hell in his mind;
And then he went to a church that had been consecrated in honour of the blessed Mary. There, with weeping and fasting, he begged for her help and intercession for a long time,
until she herself came to him in great glory and said that she had interceded for him with the Heavenly Judge, her own Son.
We also want to tell you about the end of the wicked enemy of God, Julian.
There was a holy bishop called Basil, who studied in a school together with that same Julian.
It happened that Basil was chosen as bishop of a city called Cappadocia, and Julian became emperor, even though he had earlier been tonsured as a priest.
Julian then began to love idol worship. He renounced his Christianity, practised paganism wholeheartedly, and forced his people to do the same.
Then on one occasion he set out with an army against the Persian nation, and met the bishop, and said to him,
"Well, Basil, now I have surpassed you in philosophy." The bishop answered him,
"May God grant that you had practised philosophy!" And with that word he offered him, as a blessing, the same kind of gift that he himself lived on, namely three barley loaves.
Then the apostate ordered the loaves to be accepted and grass to be given to the bishop in return, and said,
"He has offered us the food of beasts; let him receive grass as his reward." Basil accepted the grass, saying,
"O emperor, truly we offered you what we ourselves eat, and in return you have given us the fodder of unreasoning beasts, not as food for us but as an insult."
Then the enemy of God threatened him and said, "When I come back from the campaign I will tear down this city and level it and turn it into ploughland, so that it bears more corn than people.
I know all about your presumption, and that of the people of this city, who at your urging broke and threw down the statue that I set up and prayed to." And with these words he went on to Persia.
Then Basil told the people of his city about the cruel emperor's threat, and he gave them the best advice, saying:
"My brothers, bring your treasures, and let us try, if we can, to win over the cruel apostate when he comes back."
Then they gladly brought him a countless heap of gold, silver and precious gems.
The bishop then received the treasures, and commanded his priests and all the people to offer their gifts in the temple that was consecrated in honour of the blessed Mary,
And he told them to wait inside there with a three-day fast, so that the Almighty Ruler, through his mother's intercession, would overturn the wicked emperor's plans.

Then on the third night of the fast the bishop saw a great heavenly host on every side of the church, and in the midst of the host sat the heavenly queen Mary, and she said to those standing around her,
"Summon the martyr Mercurius to me, so that he may go against the wicked apostate Julian and kill him, who with a proud heart despises God, my Son."
The holy confessor Mercurius came quickly, armed, and went off at her command.
Then the bishop went into the other church, where the martyr lay, and asked the church-warden where the saint's weapons were.
He swore that he had certainly seen them at his head in the evening. And the bishop went straight to Saint Mary's church and told the people about his vision and about the cruel man's death.
Then he went back again to the holy martyr's tomb, and found his spear standing there smeared with blood.

Then three days later one of the emperor's thegns, named Libanius, came and threw himself at the bishop's feet, asking for baptism. He told him and all the people of the city about the death of the wicked Julian:
said that the army was camped by the river Euphrates, and seven sentries kept watch over the emperor.
An unknown warrior came striding up and ran him through savagely, and at once vanished from their sight; and Julian then died with a terrible cry.
So the people of the city were saved from the enemy of God through Saint Mary.

Then the bishop offered the people of the city their treasures back, but they said they would much rather give these gifts to the immortal King, who had saved them so mightily, than to the mortal killer.
However, the bishop compelled the people to accept a third of the money, and with the other two-thirds he endowed the monastery.
If anyone wonders how this came about, we say that this martyr lived his life as a layman. He was martyred for his faith in Christ during the persecution by the heathens.
Afterwards Christians laid his holy body to rest with honour inside the church, together with his weapons.
Then, when the holy queen sent him, as we said a little earlier, his spirit went swiftly, and with a physical weapon stabbed the enemy of God while his sentries looked on.
My dearest brothers, let us call with constant prayers to the holy Mother of God, that she may intercede for us with her Son in our needs.
It is very believable that he will grant her a great thing, he who humbled himself so that through her, for the redemption of the world,
he was born as a human being, he who is ever God without beginning, and now continues, in one person, true man and true God, forever in eternity.
Just as each man exists in soul and in body as one man, so Christ is God and man, one Saviour, who lives and reigns with the Father and the Holy Spirit for ever and ever. Amen.
